hypothesis.title: A record caused by a post-fault client operation waits at a restarted destination until that node has heard back from a majority of the peers its restart addressed
hypothesis.description: An eligibility mask in the is_ineligible closure of schedule_runnable (core/scheduler.rs), no hold outside the queue, no swap, bounded. New SendLedger fields: opening_peers: u64 (bitmask of remote destinations of Records the node sent while its trigger was HandlerTrigger::None and its incarnation was above zero, set in State::net_enter; that is the restart segment before any handler entry), opening_replied: u64 (set at the delivery site after exec when a message entry at D from origin O's current incarnation wrote D's state and O's bit is in D's opening_peers), both cleared in crash_node and opening_peers reset in recover_crashed_node. settled(D) = opening_peers == 0 or 2 * popcount(opening_replied & opening_peers) > popcount(opening_peers). On a treated run (own salt REQWAIT, probes exempt, bit requestWaitsForSettle = 1 << 29 on the retired 536870912 row) a Runnable::Record r with r.origin_node != r.node, r.node a server D with incarnation(D) > 0, !settled(D), current_step < D.last_restart_step + Q (Q the learned ghost-lag quantile the ghost release already reads for the run's scope, 71 on the cache; 32 when no bound is learned) and client_anchor.caused_post_fault(r.causal_operation_id) is ineligible. Lift: before building QueueInfo the closure is evaluated once over every queue; if no runnable at all is eligible with the mask, the mask is off for this step and the lift is counted, so no step goes unfilled and no run reads as a deadlock. ChannelSends, timers, faults, ghosts, opening replies and records not caused by a post-fault operation are never masked. Counters under request_wait: masked_offers, records_masked (distinct record keys), released_settled, released_bound, released_lifted, hold_steps_sum, settle_steps_hist (steps from restart to settled, both halves), and per-cell {treated, untreated} request_entries_at_restarted and request_entries_at_restarted_acted. No config field.
buildsOn: send ledger trigger and incarnation bookkeeping
opening-round-first-at-recovering-receiver (kept design, narrowed here to the request-caused class and made cost 0 by deriving the opening from the ledger)
hypothesis.rationale: Generic reading of the chain (rootAnchoredPrefix in traceanalyzer/metrics/dagorder/matching.go counts a chain from the root with every predecessor matched and earlier; write/read labels match client Invocation rows, deliver labels match handler enters, acted or not). Label 10: a client write invoked at the never-restarted node N0 (the only server that took no fault-crossing delivery on the path) after the second-restarted node N2's two dead-incarnation records (its stranded reaction, labels 8-9) entered the first-restarted node N1, with both restarts done. For the path to continue N0 must still hold its pre-fault role, so four records addressed to N0 must be undelivered at label 10 and stay undelivered through label 11: N1's dead-incarnation stranded fan-out sibling (sent with label 4's record), N2's dead-incarnation stranded-reaction sibling (sent at label 4's reaction), N1's current-incarnation reaction to the label-8 ghost, and N1's current-incarnation completion broadcast sent when label 9 acted. Label 11: N2's current-incarnation reply to the write's replication record, entered at N0. Side witnesses that must have entered N2 earlier: N1's current-incarnation recovery reply (sent at label 7, before N1's ghost-driven reaction) and N0's recovery reply (sent after N2's opening request landed at N0). For the reply to exist at all both must have ACTED at N2 before the write's replication record entered N2, and none of N1's later current-incarnation sends to N2 (reaction, broadcast) may have acted at N2 between its recovery completion and that record. Label 12: N1's current-incarnation completion broadcast entered at N0 after label 11; it was sent before label 10 and must survive undelivered across 10 and 11. Label 13: a read invoked at any server after label 12. Cache ladder: 2674 -> 423 -> 59 -> 40 -> 15, so 9->10 0.158, 10->11 0.139, 11->12 0.68, 12->13 0.375. The other half of the 10->11 loss sits at N2: the reply of label 11 exists only if the write's replication record acted at N2 after both recovery replies acted there; a request-caused record entering a node still rebuilding its state is dropped on every protocol that ignores traffic while recovering, and the drop is invisible to the ladder (entries, not effects, are matched) until the missing reply fails label 11. The DAG carries this order as the two co-predecessors of the reply: deliver_rr_1_to_2 and deliver_rr_0_to_2 both precede deliver_pok_2_to_0, and the pok is caused by the replication record acting, so the recovering-receiver-admission entry's objection (no DAG edge) does not apply to the request-caused class. The tree has nothing here: fresh_first orders dead against current records of one origin at a restarted destination, pair_order orders the dead class of one origin by ordinal, and the replication record comes from the never-crashed node while the recovery replies come from two origins. The filed reply-first read (iteration 34) found the reply and the request are rarely eligible in the same step (swaps 11,200 per chunk), which is why a same-step swap cannot carry this order and a bounded wait can. Receiver-restarted census on the cache: 4,828,168 deliveries at restarted destinations, acted 5,570 (0.0012), with zero acted at distance 0-2 and one at distance 3 of 2,060,131 deliveries, so entries into a restarted node in its first four handler entries do nothing on this protocol; the wait moves request-caused entries past that window only while the node is unsettled. Grounding for the floor: post-fault ops about 1.5 per run become ready after the first crash (merged entry), each fanning out at least two server-to-server records, 2.1 recoveries per run (1,583,194 / 757,560), an opening of tens of steps in a run of about 1,740 steps (1,318,696,077 / 757,560), so tens of thousands of request-caused records per chunk meet an unsettled restarted destination.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: A node that came back from a crash and asked its peers for state does not take a client-caused message until a majority of those peers have answered it, for at most the learned ghost-lag scale. The predicate uses only ledger facts (which peers the restart segment wrote to, which of them produced an acted entry since) and the run's causal ids; a protocol whose restart sends nothing (state persisted, Raft-style) has an empty opening and the mask is inert there, so nothing is imposed on protocols that do not recover by asking. The bound is the learned quantile the tree already carries, read per scope, and the lift keeps every step filled.

prediction.applicabilityGate: Chunk 1, before any rung is credited: add request_wait.arrivals_after_bound (request-caused records entering an unsettled restarted destination at or after last_restart_step + Q, never masked) and require records_masked / (records_masked + arrivals_after_bound) >= 0.40; below 0.40 the bound-from-restart clock misses the class and the round files that finding instead of reading a rung.
prediction.decisiveRead: Chunk 1: request_wait.cells.treated.request_entries_at_restarted_acted / request_entries_at_restarted >= 1.3x the untreated cell's, and released_settled >= released_bound. Then depth>=11 treated/untreated per run, probe-free, co-bit matched, pooled over up to four chunks (two minimum): decided only if the z-2.7 interval clears 1.00 with the point >= 1.30; an interval straddling 1.00 after four chunks is unresolved, not a confirmation.
prediction.guards: depth>=8 per run treated/untreated in [0.96, 1.04]; depth>=6 in [0.98, 1.02]; released_lifted <= 0.02 of masked_offers; settle_steps_hist median below Q on both halves; steps per run treated/untreated in [0.99, 1.02].
prediction.falsifier: With the floor and the applicability gate met: the treated acted ratio not above 1.15x the untreated; or released_bound > released_settled; or depth>=8 below 0.96; or the pooled depth>=11 interval entirely below 1.00 over four chunks.

hypothesis.redTeam: The mask applies only while current_step < D.last_restart_step + Q (71 on the cache), a clock that starts at the restart, not at the record's arrival. On the chain the write (label 10) is a post-fault operation deferred by the merged client release and issued after label 9, which follows the first acted ghost entry whose lag from the restart reads p50 31 / p75 71 / p90 151; so on a large share of depth-10 runs the replication record reaches N2 after restart+Q and the mask is inert exactly where the conversion is claimed. Where it fires, the conversion needs both recovery replies to exist and act inside the same window; if the first-restarted node dropped the opening request the wait ends on the bound as a blind delay. Depth>=11 carries 59 events per chunk on the cache (about 29 per half), so [1.10, 1.55] is not separable in two chunks and only a 2x lean is. The acted-ratio observable can rise without touching the chain (any request-caused record that waited lands on a settled node and acts). The pre-pass over every queue on treated steps is a hot-path cost with no wall counter of its own.
hypothesis.scoreReason: Clear mechanism-to-observable path with the checkable claims verified: the oracle DAG carries deliver_rr_1_to_2 and deliver_rr_0_to_2 as direct predecessors of deliver_pok_2_to_0, and the prefix walk (rootAnchoredPrefix) requires every predecessor assigned and earlier, so the order the mask enforces is the ladder's own 10->11 condition at the second-restarted node; the cross-origin contest at a restarted destination (the never-crashed node's replication record against replies from two origins) is untouched by fresh_first (same-origin class) and pair_order (exits for never-crashed origins, scheduler.rs:1997); the filed reply-first read (iteration 34, swaps 11,200 per chunk) showed the same-step form cannot carry it. It narrows the kept opening-round-first design to request-caused records, so the mutual-hold objection (the second-restarted node's fresh opening request held at the first-restarted node) no longer applies, and derives the opening from the ledger so exec.rs is untouched (cost 0 where the parent was cost 2). Eligibility mask only: no purgatory, no stall-clock interaction, bounded by the learned quantile, per-step lift stated, counters and floor stated. Not the closed orphan family: anchor is a restarted destination's unsettled opening, held class is request-caused records only, release is the settle predicate, bound is from the restart.

originalPrediction.mechanism: Treatment bit requestWaitsForSettle = 1 << 29 in run_variant.rs and VARIANT_BITS (row 536870912 renamed), own salt, treated share about 0.49 of runs by id. Depth>=8 flat: the masked class is request-caused records only, ghosts and recovery replies are untouched, so labels 4 through 9 are unchanged. Depth>=11 up because on the treated depth-10 runs where the replication record reaches N2 before N2 settled (its recovery replies from N1, sent at label 7, and from N0 have not both acted) the record now waits and acts after them, producing the reply the rung needs; the share of depth-10 runs in that state is the conversion this bit can recover, estimated a quarter to a third of the 0.139 loss. Shared-state reasoning: the mask only reorders within the network queue, the record stays eligible for everything else, a settled destination frees it at once, the ghost-lag bound frees it otherwise, and the per-step lift means a step is never left with nothing to run.
originalPrediction.independentObservable: Per cell at run end: request_wait.cells.treated.request_entries_at_restarted_acted / request_entries_at_restarted >= 1.3 x the untreated cell's ratio (a request-caused entry that waits for the settle acts where the untreated one is dropped), and request_wait.released_settled >= request_wait.released_bound (the settle, not the bound, ends most waits; settle_steps_hist median below Q on both halves).

pairedHypothesis.title: At a post-fault client operation's target, fault-touched records already in flight are held in purgatory until the operation's response leaves the target
pairedHypothesis.description: Purgatory keyed on an event class instead of the inert probability. In path.rs invoke_client_request, when post_fault is true, the run is treated (own salt OPSHELTR, run-cap and timer-context probes exempt, bit opTargetShelter = 1 << 26 on the retired 67108864 row), the target server T is not in its own restart opening (never restarted, or has an acted delivery-triggered entry since its last restart) and T's ledger has crash_pending == 0: scan state.network_queue once for Runnable::Record r with r.node == T, r.origin_node != T, origin a server, and either (a) state.fault_crossing(origin, r.origin_incarnation) (dead incarnation or origin down) or (b) incarnation(origin) > 0, r.origin_incarnation current, and r.send_ordinal >= origin's opening_end (a new SendLedger field: `issued` at the origin's first handler entry after its last restart; unset means every current record is an opening send and is left alone). Each such record is removed with take_network and moved with delay_runnable(step + 192, record) tagged with a new DeliveryBias::SHELTERED bit and keyed on the op id in a small per-run table {op_id -> Vec<record key>}. Release: (1) at ScheduleResult::ClientOp(result) whose unique_id is the op, or when the stall release settles the op, every sheltered record of that op gets release_step = current step (release_from_purgatory pushes it back next step through push_runnable, so net_enter re-counts it stale or fresh); (2) at the step start, when the network queue, every local queue and the timer queue hold nothing eligible, every sheltered record is released (dry release); (3) the 192-step bound. Records sent after the invocation are never touched; ChannelSends, client-origin records and records to other destinations are never touched. Counters in util_stats.rs under shelter: ops_examined, ops_sheltered, records_ghost, records_settled_fresh, released_on_response, released_on_expiry, released_dry, hold_steps_sum, skipped_target_opening, skipped_target_crash_pending, and per-cell {treated, untreated} sender_restarted_entries and sender_restarted_acted read at the delivery site. No config field.
pairedHypothesis.rationale: Generic reading of the chain (rootAnchoredPrefix in traceanalyzer/metrics/dagorder/matching.go counts a chain from the root with every predecessor matched and earlier; write/read labels match client Invocation rows, deliver labels match handler enters, acted or not). Label 10: a client write invoked at the never-restarted node N0 (the only server that took no fault-crossing delivery on the path) after the second-restarted node N2's two dead-incarnation records (its stranded reaction, labels 8-9) entered the first-restarted node N1, with both restarts done. For the path to continue N0 must still hold its pre-fault role, so four records addressed to N0 must be undelivered at label 10 and stay undelivered through label 11: N1's dead-incarnation stranded fan-out sibling (sent with label 4's record), N2's dead-incarnation stranded-reaction sibling (sent at label 4's reaction), N1's current-incarnation reaction to the label-8 ghost, and N1's current-incarnation completion broadcast sent when label 9 acted. Label 11: N2's current-incarnation reply to the write's replication record, entered at N0. Side witnesses that must have entered N2 earlier: N1's current-incarnation recovery reply (sent at label 7, before N1's ghost-driven reaction) and N0's recovery reply (sent after N2's opening request landed at N0). For the reply to exist at all both must have ACTED at N2 before the write's replication record entered N2, and none of N1's later current-incarnation sends to N2 (reaction, broadcast) may have acted at N2 between its recovery completion and that record. Label 12: N1's current-incarnation completion broadcast entered at N0 after label 11; it was sent before label 10 and must survive undelivered across 10 and 11. Label 13: a read invoked at any server after label 12. Cache ladder: 2674 -> 423 -> 59 -> 40 -> 15, so 9->10 0.158, 10->11 0.139, 11->12 0.68, 12->13 0.375. The 10->11 loss at N0 is the survival of four records across the whole window from their send (labels 3, 4, 8, 9) to the reply's entry after label 11; nothing on the tree orders anything at a never-restarted destination (fresh_first.skipped_never_restarted_dest 601,449 per chunk is the rule declining exactly this destination class; pair_order exits for never-crashed origins and suppresses the fresh class, corrections_fresh_suppressed 2,199,371), and the sender-preference family closed both ways (0.738 and 0.949). The shelter makes the constraint hold by construction on every treated depth-10 run where the four records are still in flight at the invocation: dead records fall in class (a), N1's reaction and broadcast in class (b) since N1's opening_end is set at its first entry after restart and both were sent by later segments; N2's opening request to N0, if still in flight, is an opening send and is not held, so N0's recovery reply (a label-11 witness) is never blocked. Release at the response also serves 11->12: N1's broadcast, held through the reply's entry, is released the step the write's response leaves N0. The orphan family (iteration 18) showed blind ghost delays from the crash cost depth>=6 (0.82): this hold starts only at a post-fault invocation and only at its target, and the crash_pending exemption keeps it off the node the plan is about to crash (the label-4 destination), so the chain's early ghost deliveries are untouched. The 192-step bound is three times the request hold's EXPIRY_STEPS and above the stock first-delivery distance of the op's own record (client_anchor first_delivery_distance stock 1,884,080 / 70,474 = 26.7 steps, hold 15.6, rush 8.1) plus a replication round trip; another protocol reads shelter.released_on_expiry / ops_sheltered: above 0.5 means its operations outlast the bound and the bound is too short there, so the value is diagnosed from the counter, not tuned. Grounding for the floor: post-fault ops per run about 2.8 (client_anchor.axis.rush.ops 206,241 on 72,988 rush runs), stale deliveries per run about 5.4 (sender_restarted 4,125,894 / 757,560), so a fault-touched record to the target is in flight at a fair share of invocations.
pairedHypothesis.generalityArgument: Stated without any handler or role name: a coordinator that receives a client request while messages touched by a fault (sent by an incarnation that died, or by a peer that restarted and has since moved on from its recovery) are on their way to it serves the request before that news arrives. This is the canonical stale-coordinator schedule (old leader commits before learning of the new view; a node acts on a request before hearing the recovery news) that stale-leader and split-brain bugs in every consensus family need, and a real network can delay any message arbitrarily, so no protocol-specific assumption is added. The mechanism has no knob: the class is defined by incarnation and ledger facts every run carries, the bound is diagnosed by an exported ratio, and the dry release keeps every run live.

pairedHypothesis.notes: Bit rows free on the merged tree: 1 << 26 and 1 << 29. This hypothesis takes 1 << 26 alone. If the session wants a nested ghost-only cut (class (a) only, class (b) left in the queue) it takes 1 << 29 and then no other proposal of this round can join the session; the recommended session is this bit crossed with request-caused-record-waits-for-restarted-target-settle on 1 << 29, each read on its own contrast matched on the other. Implementer notes: take_network then delay_runnable keeps in_flight and net_records exact (take_network does flight_leave and net_leave; delay_runnable does flight_enter; release_from_purgatory does flight_leave then push_runnable); pending_deliveries_to already counts purgatory, so the timer-context features see the held records. The single-release cell's stale-mark ranking flaw noted at iteration 81 is untouched.
pairedHypothesis.redTeam: The nearest prior is not the orphan family the proposal cites but the causal-window CLIENT_FIRST arm (iteration 63), which it never mentions: while a post-fault operation was outstanding that arm masked every same-role remote record with no post-fault cause at every destination (replies to the destination's current incarnation and restart sends exempt), a superset of this hold, and read cross-binary flat at every rung with the within-binary deep tail down (depth>=11 6 against 19, depth>=12 3 against 15, depth>=13 0 against 5). The one thing this candidate changes there is the release: response-keyed with a 192 bound, where CLIENT_FIRST closed 0.81 of its windows on its 64-step cap before the response, so its held broadcast was freed mid-round-trip; that is a real premise but not the one argued. Second: purgatory rows suspend the stall clock (path.rs:1128 tests !purgatory.is_empty()), so a 192-step shelter at a wedged target keeps the stall cap from firing and lengthens the 35 percent of runs that end on it; the 'composition only, steps within [0.98, 1.02]' claim is false as designed. Third: any post-fault read invoked at the first-restarted node between labels 7 and 9 shelters the chain's own ghosts (labels 8-9) for up to the response or 192 steps; the crash_pending exemption protects only label 4's destination. Fourth: depth>=11 at about 29 events per half per chunk resolves only a 2x lean. Fifth: three of the four 'hazards' at N0 are DAG records ordered after the reply; the fourth (N1's post-restart reaction broadcast) is a protocol inference the DAG does not carry.
pairedHypothesis.scoreReason: Explicit mechanism-to-observable path and every plumbing and counter claim verified (take_network then delay_runnable keeps in_flight exact, release_from_purgatory does flight_leave then push_runnable so net_enter re-classes the record, all_queues_empty and pending_deliveries_to count purgatory, EXPIRY_STEPS 64, the fresh_first and pair_order counters, the ladder, the first-delivery distances). The response-keyed release is a genuine new premise against the CLIENT_FIRST closure. But the proposal rests on unstated evidence that leans against it, its clean-composition claim is contradicted by the stall-clock suspension, and its decisive rung is count-limited. Not the closed orphan family: the orphan hold was armed at the crash, held the victim's ghosts at every destination and released on the destination's reply; this is armed at a post-fault invocation, holds fault-touched records to that target only and releases on the operation's response. It is, however, the CLIENT_FIRST hold narrowed to the target with a different release, and the session must read it as that.

reviewSummary: Thirteen candidates, twelve kept, one rejected. The DAG reading of labels 10-13 shared by the three new candidates is correct under the prefix walk's longest-root-anchored-chain semantics (w1, allow_t1, crash_nl, svc_1_to_2, crash_2, recover_2, rec_2_to_1, svc_2_to_1, dvc_2_to_1, w2 = 10; pok_2_to_0 = 11; sv_1_to_0 = 12; the reads = 13), and every cited fresh-cache counter checks (pair_order.corrections_fresh_suppressed 2,199,371; fresh_first.skipped_never_restarted_dest 601,449; purgatory.delayed_sends 0; receiver-restarted 4,828,168 / 5,570 with the acceptance buckets exact; ladder 2674/423/59/40/15). Two design facts the proposals missed: purgatory rows suspend the stall clock (path.rs:1128), so the shelter and the backlog deferral are run-length changes as written and their rewrites exclude their rows from the suspension; and the causal-window CLIENT_FIRST arm (iteration 63) is a superset of the shelter's hold that read flat cross-binary with the deep tail down, which the shelter never cites - its response-keyed release is the one new premise against that result. The request-wait mask stands first (DAG-backed order at the second-restarted node, eligibility mask, learned bound, cost 0); the shelter pairs with it on the other side of the same 10->11 loss; the backlog deferral waits. Recommended session: requestWaitsForSettle = 1 << 29 and opTargetShelter = 1 << 26, each read on its own contrast matched on the other; no third bit. Among carried entries the stalled-runs supply figure is still false on the merged tree (267,533 stall-capped runs per chunk, not 352,842) and the phase-wait dose is rejected with its refuted parent. Bit collisions to resolve if built later: repeated release and stalled-runs both on 1 << 27; PCT's promote cell and the shelter both on 1 << 26.
